problem: Vision-only PointGoal navigation policies trained in one scene fail when appearance or semantics change (floor texture, indoor to outdoor). Existing pretrained encoders (CLIP, MAE, DINOv2), navigation-specific contrastive methods and domain randomization do not give policy-level scene transfer, and prior privileged contrastive work assumes fixed trajectories.
motivation: Scene transfer is a key barrier to deploying camera-only navigation. Geometric sensing such as LiDAR is less appearance-sensitive. It can be used as privileged supervision only at training time to shape an RGB encoder toward navigation-relevant structure, with no LiDAR needed at deployment.
key_idea: Pretrain an RGB encoder with an InfoNCE loss whose per-pair temperature is set by privileged LiDAR geometric similarity, then freeze it and train an RL policy in a different environment (cross-stage domain mismatch).
insight: The ablation shows that most of the robustness comes from cross-stage domain mismatch (+9.7 SR when added, and +3.0 SR when RL domain randomization is also used) and from the geometry-adaptive temperature (59.86 to 63.56 SR). Standard SimCLR augmentations combined with scene-invariant pairing hurt (43.07 vs 50.20 SR without augmentations). Domain randomization in RL stage does not help (63.6 to 54.3 SR), because the randomization does not cover the real shift (textured floors), whereas a frozen encoder plus a mismatched training scene acts as an implicit regularizer. Fine-tuning on the custom dataset without contrastive geometry (AE, MAE) overfits and collapses (near 0 SR).
method: Geometry-adaptive temperature: the InfoNCE temperature is per pair. Positives use a fixed alpha=0.1. Negatives use LiDAR similarity, mapped into [tau_min, tau_max]=[0.1, 10]. Geometrically similar negatives are repelled less.
LiDAR similarity: 1 minus a normalized weighted Euclidean distance between LiDAR vectors, bounded in [0,1]. Beams inside the FOV have weight 1 and weights outside decay to 0.1 via a sigmoid.

Scene-invariant pairing: positives are the same navigation configuration replayed in visually different environments with identical geometry. Data come from replaying a privileged state-based agent. No extra image augmentations are used. Encoder is ResNet-50 (ImageNet init) with a 2-layer projection head of dimension 256, batch size 8192.

Decoupled frozen-encoder RL: the encoder is frozen; a 2-layer MLP (256 hidden, no recurrence) takes the embedding, velocities and polar goal, and outputs continuous v and omega. It is trained with SAC using a geodesic-progress reward with backward and angular penalties.
Cross-stage domain mismatch (CSDM): the encoder is pretrained on the warehouse scenes and the policy is trained only in Photo-studio, which discourages reliance on scene-specific shortcuts.

GRAN multimodal dataset: iGibson TurtleBot data with RGB, LiDAR, depth and semantic masks. It has 8 environments, 36k images per environment, 20 room settings, 10 objects per room, and 126 assets in 13 categories.

setting.backbone: ResNet-50 encoder (contrastive pretrained, frozen) + 2-layer MLP SAC policy (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: Custom iGibson dataset (GRAN) for contrastive pretraining: 4 pretraining environments, about 36k images each, replayed trajectories from a privileged state-based agent (4 source models x 100 trajectories). RL in a single Photo-studio scene.
setting.observation: monocular RGB 224x224 + goal in polar coordinates + linear/angular velocity
setting.privileged: LiDAR (and replay correspondences) used only during encoder pretraining; none at test time

numbers_note: Real-world result (10 trials, 60% indoor / 40% outdoor SR) is given only in text. The ablation table reports its own SR/SPL (best 63.56/58.61) on an unspecified aggregate of test scenes.
results: The method reaches 82.6 SR (Test Simple), 77.7 SR (Hard Simple Floor) and 49.42 SR (Hard Textured Floor), against the strongest baseline in each: CL-VT 52.0, DR-CSDM 52.52 and SimCLR 45.7. Indoor/outdoor SR is 68.65/60.89 vs SimCLR 50.14 and DR-CSDM 49.82 (outdoor). Zero-shot sim2real on a Limo Pro robot got 60% indoor and 40% outdoor success over 10 trials.
limitations: Train-environment SR (83.8) is lower than pretrained baselines (~93), and the textured-floor SR is still below 50.
Simulation-only evaluation on a custom benchmark with a simple encoder (no recurrence), and only 10 real-world trials with failures on unseen obstacles and backward motion near goal.
Assumes perfect LiDAR during training and needs replay data with identical geometry across appearances; still needs goal position input.
builds_on: Contrastive learning with privileged information for agile flight (Xing et al. 2024)
